sections.h2: Which office bills and collects property tax in Cleveland County?
sections.html:
Cleveland County Tax Administration, in the county administration building at 311 East Marion Street in Shelby, appraises property and bills and collects the tax. The office phone is 704-484-4843, and its website says the doors are open from eight to five on weekdays.

The tax administrator's site describes a county of 469 square miles that includes 15 municipalities and says the office mails and collects more than 60,000 tax notices each fall. It offers a record lookup, an online payment search, an address change request and a tax estimator.

sections.h2: How often does Cleveland County revalue real property?
sections.html:
Cleveland County told owners it revalues on a four-year cycle, tighter than the eight-year ceiling in the statute. Its latest valuation date is January 1, 2025.

The county's revaluation page explains that values are set as of that date from aerial and street photography, recent sales, land records and details such as zoning, soil class and improvements. Owners received notices in mid-February 2025. An earlier revaluation took effect in 2021, and a county news release says the commissioners cut the rate from 57.0 cents per $100 to 54.75 cents afterward.

For a seller, that means the tax value on a Cleveland County parcel is pinned to January 1, 2025.

sections.h2: What rates make up a Cleveland County tax bill?
sections.html:
The County Manager's recommended 2026-2027 budget keeps the county rate at 40.5 cents per $100 of valuation. Added to a public school rate and a fire tax rate, the news release puts the total at 61.5 cents per $100.

Confirm the adopted figures and any city or town rate with the tax office, because the release describes a recommended budget and a June public hearing. Ask the tax office which school, fire and municipal rates apply to your parcel.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Cleveland County property value?
sections.html:
You can file a written appeal online, by mail or by email, or request an in-person meeting. Cleveland County does not accept an appeal by phone.

  • Online: use the appeal form on the county tax site, one form per parcel.
  • Mail: send a photocopy of the form to the Cleveland County Tax Assessor, P.O. Box 370, Shelby, NC 28151.
  • Email: tax.assessor@clevelandcountync.gov.
  • In person: complete the request form attached to your notice and call 704-484-4911 for an appointment.

Plan on at least eight weeks for a mailed decision, and note that a review can leave the value unchanged, lower it or raise it. The county accepts two reasons: the assessed value is well above market value, or the property was appraised unfairly compared with similar properties. It does not consider the size of the increase, an insurance value, a feeling that value is simply too high, or inability to pay.

Still unhappy after the informal review? Put a hearing request in writing to the Board of Equalization and Review before it adjourns; the county publishes the adjournment date in the local newspaper and on its site. The Property Tax Commission is the next stop, with a 30-day filing clock that starts when the board mails its ruling.

sections.h2: Does a higher appraisal always mean a higher Cleveland County tax bill?
sections.html:
No. The county's explanation is that a bill equals the tax value multiplied by the rate, and each taxing jurisdiction sets its own rate. After a revaluation some bills rise, some fall and some stay about the same.

The tax office says it can only act on the appraised value. Concerns about service levels or affordability belong with the elected boards that set rates, not with the appraisers. Before you appeal, open the county's assessment records map and turn on the Improved Sales and Vacant Sales layers, which the county recommends for finding recent comparable sales near your parcel. Personal property such as vehicles, trailers and boats is valued every year, while land and buildings are valued only at a countywide revaluation.

sections.h2: Which tax relief programs does Cleveland County offer?
sections.html:
The county tax assessor takes applications for three state programs. June 1 is the usual cutoff, and an owner may draw from just one program.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: $25,000 or half the home's appraised value, whichever is bigger, comes off the taxable amount. The 2026 income ceiling is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 of appraised value is exempt, and the state form says no age or income test applies.
  • Circuit breaker: a 4 percent of income cap, or 5 percent for households between the limit and $58,200 in 2026. It requires five years of ownership and residence and a new application every year.

Deferred circuit breaker taxes for the prior three years come due if the home is transferred, so a sale ends the deferral and puts those taxes on the closing statement. The county also describes a present-use deferral for farm and forest land, which taxes at use value but keeps the deferred amount on the books.

sections.h2: What happens when a Cleveland County tax bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
September 1 is the due date, with January 5 as the last interest-free day. The 2025 relief notice said bills would be calculated and mailed in July after the rate-setting boards act.

Interest of 2 percent attaches January 6, and three-fourths of 1 percent more builds each month from February 1. The lien is on the parcel from the listing date, which means an unpaid year stays with the house.

When a county forecloses for unpaid tax, the county's tax foreclosure page shows the process. Auctions take place in the Commissioners' Room, second floor, and the top bidder puts down 5 percent. A challenger must outbid by $750 or 5 percent, whichever is larger, filing in person at the courthouse, and every upset bid restarts a ten-day clock. Redemption by the owner stays open until the court confirms.

sections.h2: How is unpaid tax handled in a Cleveland County closing?
sections.html:
Ask the collector for a payoff figure, then have the settlement agent pay it out of the seller's proceeds so the buyer does not inherit it.

Past-due years are cleared at closing along with interest. If a parcel is already in foreclosure, the county's page says liens against it can be found in the complaint in the clerk's file, and you need the CV file number to pull it at the courthouse at 100 Justice Place in Shelby.

sections.h2: What do federal figures show for housing in Cleveland County?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts shows 103,325 residents in July 2025 and 45,667 housing units. For 2020 to 2024, 70.9 percent of occupied homes are owner-held, the median value is $200,000, and median owner costs with a mortgage are $1,257 a month.

Rent has a median of $914, and the county recorded 555 permits in 2025. Persons in poverty make up 16.3 percent of the population.

faqs.q: When must a Cleveland County bill be paid?
faqs.a: By September 1; paying after January 5 adds 2 percent, then three-fourths of 1 percent for each month that follows beginning in February.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Cleveland County appraisal?
faqs.a: File a written appeal online, by mail to P.O. Box 370, Shelby, or by email, or ask for an in-person appointment at 704-484-4911. The county does not take appeals by phone, and a mailed decision can take at least eight weeks.

faqs.q: Is Cleveland County on the standard eight-year cycle?
faqs.a: No. The statute caps the gap at eight years, but the county reports a four-year cycle, and its latest revaluation took effect January 1, 2025.

faqs.q: By when must relief paperwork reach the county?
faqs.a: The county sets June 1 as the usual deadline for the tax year. The elderly or disabled exclusion, disabled veteran exclusion and circuit breaker are all filed with the county, not the Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: May I close on a Cleveland County sale while taxes are owed?
faqs.a: Yes. Get the balance from the collector and have it paid out of your proceeds. If the county has started a foreclosure, you can still redeem until the court confirms the sale.
